title: New pt L5-S1 HNP, left S1 radiculopathy (real GPT note from prod)
note:
SUBJECTIVE:
42-year-old male, new to practice, presents with three months of low back pain radiating down the left leg to the lateral foot. Reports numbness in the left lateral foot and weakness with plantar flexion. No other systemic complaints documented. New patient; outside MRI reviewed.

OBJECTIVE:
- Neuro/musculoskeletal exam:
  - Positive straight leg raise on the left at 40 degrees.
  - Diminished left Achilles (S1) reflex.
  - Left gastrocnemius (plantar flexion) strength 4/5.
- Imaging:
  - Outside lumbar spine MRI reviewed: large left paracentral L5–S1 disc herniation compressing the left S1 nerve root.

ASSESSMENT:
1. Lumbar disc herniation at L5–S1 with left S1 radiculopathy — consistent with history, exam, and MRI findings.

PLAN:
- Initiate physical therapy focused on lumbar stabilization, core strengthening, and radicular symptom management.
- Start Medrol dose pack (methylprednisolone taper) for short course anti-inflammatory therapy.
- Refer for left L5–S1 transforaminal epidural steroid injection for targeted radicular pain control.
- Advise return/follow-up in 6 weeks to reassess symptoms, strength, and reflexes; sooner if worsening neurological deficits, progressive weakness, or bowel/bladder dysfunction.
- Documented moderate complexity medical decision making.
